name: Deuce-To-Seven Lowball
description: Deuce-to-Seven Lowball (also called Kansas City Lowball or Billy Baxter Lowball) is a draw poker variant where the lowest hand wins. Aces are always high, straights and flushes count against the player, and the best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 (hence 'Deuce to Seven'). It is the exact opposite of standard high poker except for the A-2-3-4-5 rule.

history.cultural: Deuce-to-Seven is considered a 'pure' poker game favored by professionals due to its complexity and the skill required to play well. It's often included in mixed games like HORSE.
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard lowball poker with the specific ranking system that makes 7-5-4-3-2 the nuts. Multiple draw variants (single, double, triple) developed to add complexity and action.

rules.objective: Make the lowest possible five-card hand. The best hand is 7-5-4-3-2 (no flush). Straights and flushes count against you, and aces are always high.
rules.gameplay:
SINGLE DRAW VERSION:
1. Dealer deals 5 cards to each player
2. First betting round (beginning left of blinds)
3. Players may discard 0-5 cards and receive replacements
4. Second betting round
5. Showdown - lowest hand wins

TRIPLE DRAW VERSION:
1. Deal 5 cards to each player
2. First betting round
3. First draw (discard and replace)
4. Second betting round
5. Second draw
6. Third betting round
7. Third draw
8. Final betting round
9. Showdown

Note: If dealer runs out of cards during multiple draws, discards are shuffled to form new deck
keyRules: Aces are ALWAYS high (A-2-3-4-5 is NOT a straight, but ace makes it a poor hand)
Straights and flushes count against you (bad hands to have)
Best hand is 7-5-4-3-2 with mixed suits (no straight, no flush)
When comparing hands, look at highest card first
Paired cards always make hands worse

strategy.basic:
Learn the hand rankings thoroughly - 7-5-4-3-2 is the nuts
Understand that straights and flushes are bad
Remember aces are always high (bad cards)
Drawing more than one card is risky due to pairing probability
strategy.intermediate:
When drawing to a five-card hand, seldom draw more than one card
If you draw two cards, you'll make a pair about 50% of the time
Chance of making 9-high or better is never more than 25% when drawing two
Position matters - act last for maximum information
strategy.advanced:
Triple draw strategy: can draw more cards on first draw, but stand pat or draw one on final draw
Bluffing with pat hands (no draw)
Reading opponents' draw patterns
Pot odds calculations for drawing decisions
Mixed game strategy when Deuce-to-Seven is one of several games
tips: Drawing two cards makes a pair about half the time - be cautious
With three low cards, your chance of making 9-high or better is under 25%
In triple draw, you can be more aggressive with draws early, but conservative on final draw
A pat hand (standing pat) can be a powerful bluffing tool
Watch opponents' number of cards drawn for information

variations.name: Deuce to Seven Triple Draw
variations.description: Players have three opportunities to discard and draw. After deal, first betting round; first draw and second betting round; second draw and third betting round; third draw and fourth betting round; then showdown. In fixed limit, bet size normally doubles after the second draw. When the dealer runs out of cards, discards are shuffled to form a new deck for replacements.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Triple draw uses same engine constants; no overrides needed for this variant.

variations.description: Similar to Triple Draw but players have only two draw opportunities. Three betting rounds: after the deal, after the first draw, and after the second draw. Same deuce-to-seven hand ranking at showdown.
